A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same concept-shift analysis and multimodal steering framework. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning and concept-recovery experiments, VQAv2 steering results, COCO captioning results and extensive appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds expanded concept-recovery evaluations, gender-neutral captioning experiments and multimodal safety evaluations.

M1.justification: The core K-means concept extraction, mean-shift recovery and additive steering procedures remain. v2 adds application-specific adaptations: nearest-neutral concept matching with token-dependent steering in Appendix C, and safety-vector construction from unsafe image-conditioned responses versus safe text-conditioned responses in Appendix D.

E1.justification: v2 adds gender-neutral captioning on COCO and safety evaluation on MM-SafetyBench, including harmful requests, prevention requests and image-versus-blank-image conditions. These substantially extend the task requirements beyond v1's retained Visual Genome specialization, VQAv2 answer steering and COCO caption-style steering.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 introduces a direct coarse-versus-fine-grained steering comparison for gender debiasing; v1 reported these steering approaches separately without this head-to-head evaluation. Existing VQA comparisons remain unchanged. Newly discussed methods such as ReFT and AdaShield are cited, not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: New protocols include gender-word filtering and conversion scoring, plus refusal-string safety evaluation across seven MM-SafetyBench categories, a 733-example modality comparison and 100-query harmful and prevention evaluations. Concept recovery is also evaluated across more target tokens, with consistency-recovery correlations spanning four tokens. Promoting LLaVA from appendix to main text does not itself introduce a new model setting.

E4.justification: v1's magnitude-recovery and magnitude-consistency analyses are replaced by direct consistency-recovery tests across four tokens (v2 Figures 7 and 17). Gender-steering case studies and safety controls are added. The task-keyword specialization sweep, several color-steering ablation rows and multi-concept captioning analyses are removed, while most existing steering ablations remain.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 6 summarizes recovery using means and standard deviations over 20 concepts per token, replacing the earlier per-concept presentation. Pearson correlations and p-values already appeared in v1, whose shift-magnitude dispersion summaries are removed. Neither version specifies repeated experimental runs or seeds.

E6.justification: New results include 232 coarse versus 632 fine-grained gender-neutral conversions for LLaVA (v2 Table 4), and Qwen2-VL harmful non-refusal counts of 45/100 before versus 5/100 after safety steering (Table 5). These are newly reported experiments, not gains over v1 under matched settings. Tables 1–3 and the multi-model VQA table are numerically unchanged; recovery results expand and some appendix result entries disappear.

T1.justification: The grounding, concept-recovery, shift-consistency and optimal-transport mathematics are retained. The consistency formula in v2's main text already appeared in v1 Appendix A.5. New application equations specialize existing cosine matching and additive steering, while the ASR formula documents an evaluation metric. No new theorem, proof or substantive formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the contribution to a framework for interpreting and controlling concepts across fine-tuning and datasets, with demonstrated gender debiasing and safety control. v1 emphasized representation evolution and answer/style manipulation, treating debiasing and safety as future extensions. Its explicit claim to be the first work exploring MLLM steering is removed.

C2.justification: v2 directly relates recovery to shift consistency instead of explaining it through shift magnitude, and adds a limitation concerning nonlinear features. New interpretations address contextual neutralization, model-specific safety behavior and false refusals from keyword matching. Earlier steering-strength and response-quality tradeoffs remain in Appendix B. Appendix D also introduces conflicting statements about whether higher or lower ASR indicates better safety.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D add gendered/neutral word lists, filtering rules, K=5, model-specific sample counts, refusal strings, query construction and safety steering at layer 19 with alpha=1. The advertised code link changes from a repository to a project/code page. Existing LoRA settings remain, although v1's explicit OPT-based single-task architecture description is no longer spelled out.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of multimodal in-context learning and task-vector approaches, contrasting their demonstration and training requirements with concept-level steering. Safety and nonlinear-feature references are added, including ETA, FigStep, AdaShield and Not All Language Model Features Are Linear. The foundational positioning around CoX-LMM and representation editing largely remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Material previously divided among background, fine-tuning analysis and steering sections is reorganized into a unified Methodology Overview followed by Experiments. The appendices are substantially reorganized, with new C–D sections and changed placement of model-specific analyses.

P2.justification: v2 merges the analysis and steering diagrams into Figure 1, replaces several concept illustrations, changes recovery charts to per-token summaries and adds a t-SNE visualization and application tables. Numerous appendix panels are removed or repacked. The swapped concept-count and extraction-layer captions in v1 Figures 17–18 are corrected in v2 Figures 15–16.

improvement.justification: The broader recovery evidence and direct consistency analysis strengthen the recovery explanation, while clearer organization and new application tests improve on v1's largely illustrative steering demonstrations. The gains are limited by removed supplementary analyses and weaknesses in the new safety reporting: refusal strings are an imperfect proxy, and Appendix D contradicts its own ASR definition and direction. Overall, v2 provides better-supported analysis and practical evidence, but its broad safety claims remain insufficiently qualified.
